name: MonarchNumberInput
title: NumberInput
summary: A labelled number field that reads and writes numbers in the person's locale, with a stepper that never drifts, helper text and an error state.
whenToUse: For a number that is typed or nudged: a quantity, a price, a percentage, a weight.
whenNotToUse: For a value picked from a small range by feel, use Slider. For a number that is only stepped and never typed, a plain Stepper in a Form is enough. For digits that are not a quantity (a phone number, a code), use MonarchTextField with a number keyboard.
api: init(_ label: String, value: Binding<Double?>, format: Format, minimum: Double? = nil, maximum: Double? = nil, step: Double = 1, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = true, rangeMessage: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) where Format: ParseableFormatStyle, Format.FormatInput == Double, Format.FormatOutput == String

init(_ label: String, value: Binding<Double?>, minimum: Double? = nil, maximum: Double? = nil, step: Double = 1, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = true, rangeMessage: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) where Format == FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or nil while the field is empty. Every edit that reads as a number is written at once, so an action tapped straight after typing reads what is shown.

options.name: format
options.default: the locale's number format, up to three fraction digits or as many as step has
options.description: How the number is shown and read, for example .percent or .currency(code:). It is given the locale of the environment.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest allowed value. Typed values below it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The largest allowed value. Typed values above it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of the stepper adds or removes.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message; replaces the helper and the range message while present.

options.name: showsStepper
options.description: Whether the − and + buttons are shown beside the field. Each is a 44-point target named "Increase <label>" and "Decrease <label>".

options.name: rangeMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in message for a value outside the bounds.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Required" and the form of an error.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is nil and the prompt shows in the subtle text colour. The first step starts from the minimum, or from 0.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Danger border, and an icon and "Enter a number from 0 to 99." under the field. The value is kept.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the range message, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The half of the stepper that would pass the bound is disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The field has the measures and colours of MonarchTextField: a surface fill, an input border and 8-point corners, with the focus ring of the theme. Digits are monospaced so the number does not shift while it is stepped. The stepper is the system control.
platformNotes: The web parses the text itself and keeps text it cannot read on screen with "Enter a number.". On iOS the field is the standard TextField(value:format:): text the format cannot parse is put back to the last value when editing ends, which is the platform behaviour, so there is no not-a-number message. The web never stores an out-of-range value; here the binding holds what was typed and the field flags it, so the app must not treat a flagged value as valid. Arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, and the largeStep option have no touch equivalent and are not offered. The − and + buttons are the system Stepper, which repeats while held; its halves are about 47 by 32 points, below the 44-point target, because the system control's size is fixed. There is no size option: the field is always at least 44 points high. The value is a Double; steps are calculated in decimal arithmetic so they do not drift.
accessibility: The field is one element: label, the formatted number as the value, then the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper as the hint.
A new error or range message is announced when it appears, and is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The stepper is the system control with the same label, the formatted number as its value, and the increment and decrement actions.
The keyboard is the decimal pad, or one with a minus sign unless the minimum rules out negative numbers.
The field is at least 44 points high and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A value between grid points steps to the next grid point in that direction: 5 with a step of 10 goes to 10 or to 0. The grid starts at the minimum, or at 0.
A step that is not positive disables the stepper.
The decimal pad has no Return key: the number is committed when focus leaves the field.
With the .percent format the value is a fraction: 0.15 shows as 15%, and a step of 0.05 moves it by five points.
Very large or very small numbers follow the format; the default shows at most three fraction digits unless the step has more.
